items.title: Ben Sidran interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 15, 2023
items.q: It reminds me of, I had a conversation with Dave Frishberg and he said, “When I write I’m writing according to the limitations of my own vocal ability.”

ctx.x: never put any time into learning to use my voice, and particularly with the microphone. You know these microphones today, you can really work with them to project a certain persona or image, they’re so sensitive that you can’t do in the real world. It’s like working with a microphone. And that’s this whole territory that opens up for you once you get into a studio.

It reminds me of, I had a conversation with Dave Frishberg and he said, “When I write I’m writing according to the limitations of my own vocal ability.” And then he said, “I bet Mose Allison would say the same thing. A lot of his songs are shaped by the way he sings.”

Yeah. I think that’s true. I know Mose also believed that he had to be playing piano in order to sing, that they were of one piece. You had to be sitting at the piano and accompanying himself when he sang.
